newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 28.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh will have to dissolve the House of Representatives by the end of this year if the Constitution Drafting Assembly's (CDA) new proposal for a political reform time-frame holds sway. The CDA's drafting committee, in wrapping up the first constitutional draft yesterday, dramatically brought forward the deadline for the existing Parliament to promulgate key laws to supplement the new charter - from 330 days after the enactment of the new Constitution to 120 days. (THE NATION, BANGKOK POST)

- Chaiwat Sinsuwong has become leader of the Palang Dharma Party uncontested after Sudarat Keyuraphan, earlier expected to be his major contender, withdrew from the race. A 24-member executive committee was also elected during yesterday's party annual assembly. (BANGKOK POST)

- At least three police officers have been found negligent in the performance of their duty in connection with the gang-rape of four Laotian women inside a prison in Rayong province. The four Laotian women, who were detained for gambling and illegal entry into Thailand, told police last week that they were raped by 15 other inmates while police were present in the station. (THE NATION)

- Bank of Thailand officials will no longer serve as board directors for commercial banks in order to protect against allegations of unfair use of insider information. Since Rerngchai Marakanond became governor last July, the central bank has changed a long-standing policy of sending officials to serve as directors for banks in which the Financial Institutions Development Fund has taken a stake. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) is concerned that mounting opposition to the construction of the pipeline from offshore gas fields in Burma to provide fuel to power plants in Ratchaburi province could delay the project. PTT is currently laying a 260 km pipeline from power plants in Ratchaburi province to the Thai-Burmese border. The project has faced opposition from a handful of local people citing its impact on the environment and safety. (BUSINESS DAY)
